ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening against FINTRAC, OSFI, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list and Canadian Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Regulations; mandatory identification of domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of state and public office holders; threshold screening at 25% beneficial ownership with additional review of control-in-fact; adverse media and politically exposed person risk rating for all UBOs; enhanced due diligence aligned with medium-risk medical manufacturing and government payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via Service Alberta’s authorized online service provider platform for NUANS searches and Articles of Incorporation filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must use Latin characters in English or French; must comprise a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or abbreviation 'ULC'; non-Latin scripts are not accepted; corporate name search against NUANS for conflicting and confusingly similar names is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, submit a revised Name Search Report through the same registry portal; within 30 days of the rejection notice, file an administrative reconsideration request with the Registrar of Corporations citing specific statutory grounds and addressing the conflicting name or prohibited token; if the reconsideration is refused, commence judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 60 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible solely as the registered office provided the office is located in Alberta and accessible for legal process; for a ULC engaged in ISIC 3250 life-support ventilator manufacturing and targeted government procurement, a virtual office without physical commercial substance may fail substantive presence reviews; routine use of a registered agent's office is acceptable but not recommended for this industry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; s. 5 (incorporation), s. 10 (unlimited liability corporation), s. 15 (Certificate of Incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), s. 136 (first directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-01) submitted electronically through Service Alberta's Corporate Registry via authorized service provider
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; an Alberta ULC may incorporate with capital paid for in cash or property as determined by the incorporators; no escrow account is statutorily required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the corporation adopt the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry; that the initial registered office be [insert address], Alberta; that [Name] be appointed Director and President, [Name] CFO, [Name] Corporate Secretary; that the directors approve the issue of one common share to [Subscriber] for lawful consideration paid for in cash, in accordance with the ULC's unlimited liability provisions; that management be authorized to open bank accounts with [Bank], to apply for CRA business registration (BN/RT-1), to maintain books and records in English, and to engage legal counsel to finalize share certificates, minute book, and governance records, effective upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Alberta NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Service Alberta (online via service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS corporate name search for the proposed ULC name, ensuring acceptable 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' suffix and no confusingly similar existing trademarks/entities. Submit online name reservation request and obtain NUANS report (valid for 90 days). If the name is removed from use or the user decides not to incorporate within 90 days, the report must be renewed or re-submitted.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
NUANS search application fee
Proof of authorized signatory identity
Proposed jurisdiction of residence of each director (name and address only)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the proposed corporate name or add a distinctive element, re-file the NUANS application, and request expedited review if the name is refused. If NUANS report is expired or contains a conflicting mark, register a new name request within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles of Incorporation for Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — online incorporation through authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Articles of Incorporation via the Government of Alberta's Corporate Registry online portal or an accredited registry agent. At minimum provide: full corporate name in English, registered office address in Alberta, number (or minimum/maximum) of directors, first director names and addresses, class of shares (e.g., common shares with full voting rights), and statement electing unlimited liability. Pay the incorporation fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation electronically from the registry.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (form INC-01 in PDF or via e-filing)
NUANS name search report (valid within 90 days)
Name reservation receipt
Director appointment consent records
Registered office address (physical street address in Alberta) and notice of address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection or query (e.g., missing director consent, share structure non-compliance, incomplete address), cure by filing an amended Articles of Incorporation within 10 business days and re-submitting fee. For refused names or invalid NUANS report, provide a new name and revised articles. If Certificate of Incorporation is not issued within SLA, escalate to Service Alberta registry helpdesk for expedited manual review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Internal Organizational and First Board Governance, Share Subscription, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate records by Board of Directors; CRA (Canada Revenue Agency) via Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the incorporator appoints first directors and convenes the first board meeting. At this meeting the board adopts by-laws, sets the financial year end, approves share issuance, designates officers (President, CFO, Secretary), appoints an auditor or waives audit if unanimous consent is given, records the registered office location, and executes banking resolution. Additionally, register for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and CRA program accounts (e.g., corporate income tax account, GST/HST if taxable, payroll if employees are hired) using CRA's Business Registration Online.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (scan/photocopy)
Articles of Incorporation
Written resolution of sole incorporator appointing first directors
Minutes of the first board meeting
By-law No. 1 and By-law No. 2 (or consolidated by-law)
Register of directors and officers with names, addresses, nationalities
Register of registered office and records address
Share certificate(s) and transfer/issuance register
Notice of share-class details (if not included in Articles)
CRA Business Registration request (BN, RC145 if corporate income tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA BN application is rejected due to mismatched legal name or address, amend the corporate records and re-file via CRA. If a director refuses appointment, the remaining directors may act if quorum is met; if board quorum cannot be obtained, hold a written consent resolution or call a special shareholders' meeting to ratify. For missing director consents, execute fresh consents and submit to the registry if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UCC / Bulk and Miscellaneous Post-Incorporation Filings and Governance Clarification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Alberta Courts (for judicial cure if required); relevant professional/insurance bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File any required UCC-type security interest registrations (e.g., under Alberta's Personal Property Security Act if financing is taken), register beneficial ownership information under applicable federal/AB transparency rules (e.g., Federal Corporate Transparency / Canada Business Corporations Act analogues apply to federally incorporated entities, but Alberta ULCs must disclose beneficial owners in the Registry's own platform if required). Obtain any necessary professional or industry licenses for the manufacture of medical devices, including Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL). Complete post-incorporation formalities: publish notice of incorporation if contracted creditor requires it, keep the corporate minute book at the registered office, and file annual returns with Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office and records address (e.g., lease, utility bill)
Copy of director/officer consents and resignations
Notice of change of directors or address (if any)
Article amendment forms for any post-incorporation changes (e.g., share classes, registered office)
Annual return form (Alberta Corporate Registry Annual Return)
Certificate and certificate copies of all corporate files
CRA business number
Health Canada MDEL application proof (for medical device legal registration)
Municipal business licence or development permit confirming manufacturing use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return or beneficial-ownership filing is late, use Alberta MRA (my business regulations) or registry agent to submit a late-filing correction notice and pay the prescribed renewal fee. If the Alberta Registry flags potential ULC structural non-compliance, seek a curative resolution from the board and file an amended Articles of Incorporation within 30 days. For any third-party commercial registration, remedy by posting a corporate bond or indemnity pending correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate (Health Products and Food Branch); Alberta Municipal Affairs / municipal building inspection authority for manufacturing facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) and device-specific Medical Device Licence under the Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282); ISO 13485 certification is nominally voluntary but generally required for marketability

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEP) / Environmental Services Branch, Government of Alberta
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) for a proposed medical device manufacturing operation if emissions or hazardous waste volumes exceed thresholds; most assembly/light-manufacturing ventilator facilities qualify as Exempt or Category 1 (Registration) and do not require a full EIA Report. Full EIA Report is triggered only where an industrial activity is specifically listed in Schedule 1 and has significant environmental effects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and the Standards for Waste Management (Alberta Tier 1 and Tier 2 Guidelines); wastewater discharges to municipal sanitary sewer must meet municipal sewer-use bylaws and the Alberta Water Act; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must not exceed 3.0 kg/hour or 10 tonnes/year without an EPEA approval; hazardous waste must be handled, manifest, transported, and disposed of in accordance with the Waste Control Regulation (AR 192/1996) and the Storage and Handling of Dangerous Goods under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act. For ventilation-system testing, exhaust stack venting must comply with National Building Code of Canada and Alberta Building Code ventilation provisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain Alberta Building Code (ABC) compliance from municipal building safety authorities (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Safety Codes Permit); a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate per the Alberta Fire Code; structural load assessments demonstrating that the facility can support heavy HVAC or turbine-testing equipment; workplace clearance and an OHS incident prevention plan from Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (Alberta Labour); and certification of electrical / mechanical systems by a licensed professional engineer. For production of life-support equipment, the facility must also secure Health Canada establishment licensing and relevant quality-system certificates (CSAZ/ISO 13485), all subject to random inspection by Health Canada and Alberta Municipal Affairs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal corporate income tax and GST/HST administration; registration portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-registration-online.html). Provincial registry: Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry One) for the ULC incorporation. Alberta corporate income tax is assessed and collected by the CRA under the Alberta-CRA Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Alberta ULC under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (RSA 2000, c. B-9, Part 2.1) via Alberta Corporate Registry; obtain the incorporation certificate and registry number. 2) Apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) and program accounts — RP (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RC (payroll), RM (import/export) — through Business Registration Online or Form RC1, authenticating with the Alberta registry number. 3) Register for GST/HST under ETA s. 240; the CRA assigns an RT program account and the BN must be shown on every GST/HST invoice. 4) Because the ULC is presumed foreign-controlled, it is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation; the general federal rate (15%) and Alberta rate (8%) apply to taxable Canadian-source income. 5) Separate non-tax statutory licensing (Health Canada Medical Device Licence / Establishment Licence under the Food and Drugs Act) must precede commercial sale; CRA tax registration does not constitute health regulatory approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Canadian domestic law, the Alberta ULC is a corporation subject to entity-level Part I income tax (federal 15% + Alberta 8%). The 'Pass_Through_Eligible' classification derives from U.S. federal 'check-the-box' eligibility under Treasury Reg. § 301.7701-3 (Form 8832): an Alberta ULC, having unlimited liability, is an eligible entity that may elect disregarded-entity or partnership status for U.S. federal tax purposes while remaining a Canadian resident corporation. Other elections: (a) ETA s. 156 election between closely related corporations to treat intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration (non-taxable, no input tax credits); (b) GST/HST Quick Method remittance election under ETA s. 227 where annual worldwide taxable supplies do not exceed CAD 400,000; (c) entity-classification election (Form 8832) is the principal mechanism to manage hybrid status, subject to Canada's hybrid mismatch rules enacted under BEPS Action 2 (2023 Budget Implementation Act) — no separate 'hybrid mismatch election' exists under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada). Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax; only the federal 5% GST applies to supplies made in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1)(a): registration is mandatory once taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; registration must be completed within 29 days thereafter. Voluntary registration is available under ETA s. 240(4).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, government API pre-clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. A GST/HST registrant must issue sales invoices containing prescribed information (ETA s. 223; simplified invoices under s. 224) and may issue electronic invoices with the recipient's consent and acceptable records (GST/HST Memorandum 12.10). Canada's federal and provincial procurement has adopted optional e-invoicing via the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework (PEPPOL/PINT standard); buyer-driven B2B portals (EDI, Ariba, Coupa) are contractual, not statutory fiscal clearance obligations. The CRA requires invoices to show the supplier's BN/RT account and, for zero-rated exports, a statement that the supply is zero-rated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including ICU mechanical ventilators) are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 1 where the goods are sold for delivery outside Canada and are exported 'by the supplier or at the supplier's direction'. Related post-sale services (warranty, technical support, calibration) may also be zero-rated under Part V, s. 7 where supplied to a non-resident and the benefit is realized outside Canada. The ULC must be a GST/HST registrant; zero-rated exports are taxable supplies at 0%, count toward the small-supplier threshold, and preserve the right to claim input tax credits on Canadian inputs. Domestic deliveries of ventilators within Canada are generally subject to 5% GST unless a specific Part II Schedule VI medical-device zero-rating applies; export zero-rating applies irrespective of the domestic classification. Canada does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure below represents the internal documentary retention and financing-control window applied by trade-finance banks and used by CRA as an evidentiary reference for traceable export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A or CERS electronic export declaration; for U.S. land shipments, the reconciled export manifest/ACE record) naming the ULC as exporter and showing date and mode of export
Bill of Lading (ocean bill, airway bill, or truck waybill) naming the ULC as exporter or shipper; where a freight forwarder is named, a carrier certificate and CRA 'Exporter's Self-Declaration'
Commercial invoice for the exported goods plus the foreign destination customs entry or customs broker certification evidencing physical export
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT wire payment record or bank credit advice from the foreign buyer evidencing settlement in the invoiced currency
Packing list, customs value/weight summary, and the CRA GST/HST Memorandum 17.2 documentary checklist (including third-party exporter declarations where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA GST/HST reassessment window is normally four years (ETA s. 298) but becomes unlimited where a return contains misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud. Where export documentation is deficient, CRA may reassess the export revenue as taxable at 5% GST, deny related input tax credits, and assess prescribed arrears interest. Penalties: under ETA s. 280(2), knowingly making a false statement or gross negligence triggers a penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 200% of the tax sought to be evaded; criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 327 carries fines and imprisonment (up to 5 years). Additional exposure for this ULC structure: ETA s. 323 makes directors jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST, and the unlimited liability attribute of the ULC allows creditors and CRA to pursue shareholders directly for corporate GST debts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Department of Finance Canada (Canada applies a free-floating exchange-rate regime with no exchange-control agency; the Bank of Canada issues currency and manages monetary policy, while cross-border reporting is enforceable through FINTRAC and Canada Border Services Agency).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current and capital account. There are no restrictions on non-resident equity ownership, dividend streaming, or profit remittance for an Alberta ULC. No physical repatriation or surrender requirements exist. Certain informational filings may apply (FATCA/CRS under Part XVIII of the Income Tax Act; CFIUS-style review under the Investment Canada Act), and the ULC's unlimited liability and tax-transparent status must be disclosed to the bank for risk-rating purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory export-proceeds surrender, conversion, or repatriation timelines. Exporters may retain foreign exchange revenues offshore or in domestic foreign-currency bank accounts. For all export/import transactions exceeding C$10,000, the money-transfer and reporting rules require record-keeping and, where applicable, FINTRAC reports; underlying commercial documents must support the Income Tax Act and customs disclosures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to medium. No passport for EU/UK EMI licences into Canada. A fintech must be a FINTRAC-registered Money Service Business (MSB) or hold a Canadian payment-provider arrangement with a Schedule I bank. Legal constraints include the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the Retail Payment Activities Act (when in force), and bank-completion requirements. Such rails are suitable for collecting customer funds but not for capital-block escrow, government LCs, or trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Canadian Schedule I banks will allow remote video-based KYC for Canadian directors; however, for a non-resident-controlled ULC, most banks require at least one director or the ULC's authorised signatory to appear in person at an Alberta branch or before a Canadian notary for the initial banker's interview. Some institutions permit the interview by video conference for corporate clients with clean beneficial-ownership profiles and a Canadian legal counsel certificate. This mandate is not statutory on the federal level, but is imposed as bank-specific AML policy under FINTRAC guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified copy of the Alberta Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Continuance/Amalgamation, unanimous shareholder agreement, register of directors and members, non-resident ownership declaration, and a Canadian legal opinion confirming the ULC's existence, pass-through tax classification, unlimited liability implications, and authority of signatories. Source of wealth/net worth statement for every ultimate beneficial owner; bank references from home jurisdiction; audited balance sheet if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business risk / sector typology: medical apparatus manufacturing with government and hospital counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment License (MDEL), ISO 13485 certificate, CSA/UL certificates, real purchase orders or letters of intent from hospitals/distributors, export compliance declarations, product technical documentation, quality assurance manual, clinical references, and regulatory certification from the jurisdiction of final distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border wire frequency and expectation of government LC proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full treasury policy, projected cash-flow model, invoices/packing lists/bills of lading, LC drafts or copies, SWIFT counterparty authorisation list, FINTRAC/SAR framework, sanctions-screening process (including UN/OFAC/CBSA names), and evidence of no shell-company indicators (physical facilities, employees, and professional advisors).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) MT103 or MT202 from the foreign investor to the ULC's CAD-denominated account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, cleared through the Bank of Canada's Large Value Transfer System. All wires must designate a clear payment purpose, e.g. 'Capital contribution / share subscription' or 'Shareholder loan to ULC', with supporting board resolution and subscription contract. The bank will conduct funds verification against the registers of directors/shareholders and source-of-wealth files. Amounts ≥ C$10,000 must be documented; no exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational payments and supplier settlements, use SWIFT MT103 through the ULC's CAD/USD account. For government tenders and hospital procurement involving foreign buyers, issue or receive documentary letters of credit, typically under UCP600, using MT700/MT707, with negotiation at a Canadian branch or correspondent. CAD events settle via LVTS; USD clear via the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent or through CLS for FX spot legs. All trade documents must conform to Incoterms 2020 and be presented for LC negotiation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable USD/CAD forward (available offshore though not needed for CAD)
Interest rate swap/hedge for floating-rate trade finance debt, if connected to underlying exposure

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holidays; available manufacturing investment tax credits and R&D super-deduction

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Alberta Corporate Tax Return (Form T2) filed electronically via My Account or NETFILE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income from all sources adjusted for Canadian tax rules including capital cost allowance and scientific research and experimental development expenditures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source income; non-residents file T2NR if carrying on business in Alberta

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 15% of taxable income after applicable deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A unless non-resident carries on business in Alberta through a permanent establishment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $100 per month up to maximum $2,000 plus interest on unpaid tax at prescribed rate

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for most dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Treaty Relief Certificate application to Canada Revenue Agency with beneficial ownership declaration and supporting documentation; approval required prior to remittance
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced under DTAs (typically 0-5%); Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced under DTAs (typically 0-15%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 500,000 for related-party transactions triggering Local File requirement; Master File required for MNEs with consolidated group revenue exceeding CAD 50 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to entities with passive income; requires meaningful economic activities and decision-making in Canada

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of taxable income in corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction carrying fines up to CAD 1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability including possible imprisonment and restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a corporation without real business operations or economic substance in Alberta
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to CAD 100,000 and potential revocation of corporate status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil claims, disqualification from office, and personal liability for unpaid taxes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of income with penalties up to 10% of underpaid tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No personal liability but directors may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct adequate KYC or report suspicious cross-border transactions involving ventilator hardware sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 500,000 and criminal imprisonment for serious breaches
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and possible criminal charges for directors responsible for compliance
